summary: Jake Burkett chronicles more than a decade in indie game development, emphasizing a shift from chasing hits to building a sustainable, long-tail business. He threads together personal history, experimental projects, and the accumulation of revenue over time, highlighting lessons such as investing in art and audio, repromoting long-tail titles, localizing for new markets, and leveraging grants and tax credits. The talk blends hard-won experiences—facing cash flow crises, contract work versus owning titles, and collaboration with his spouse—into pragmatic strategies for resilience, community building (Full Indie), and data-informed decision making. Throughout, Burkett reinforces the idea that sustainable success comes from incremental progress, collaboration, and maintaining focus on the end goal rather than a single hit.
title: How to Survive in Gamedev for Eleven Years Without a Hit (GDC 2016)
